Narotam Singh

 Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others

Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Shivam Rana, Advocate for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Petitioner's land situate in Mauja
Barkot, District Uttarkashi was
allegedly acquired for construction of
National Highway, however,
compensation due for such land was
not paid to him.
4. By means of this writ petition,
petitioner has sought the following
reliefs:-
"(i) Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in
the nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents to prepare and pass the Award under
the National Highways Act, 1956, and to release
compensation for 0.0397 hectare of Khasra No.
560, situated in Mauza Barkot Madhya, Patti
Barkot, Tehsil Barkot, District Uttarkashi, in the
locality (tok) Chakali, which was taken over for
widening of the Dharasu-Yamunotri National

UKHC010170802026
2026:UHC:8776
Highway and which stands recorded in the
Revenue reports, obtained under the RTI reply, as
lying within the National Highway. (Contained as
Annexure No. 03 (Colly), From Page no 25 to 30)
(ii) Direct the respondents to determine and
pay compensation strictly in accordance with law,
applying the provisions of the Right to Fair
Compensation and Transparency in Land
Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013, together with all statutory benefits,
including solatium and interest from the date of
acquisition, as are now payable under the
governing legal framework.
(iii) Direct the respondents to disclose the
date on which possession of the petitioner's land
was taken, and to pay interest on the
compensation amount from that date until actual
payment, so that the petitioner is not deprived of
either his land or its price.
(iv) Declare that the continued deprivation of
the petitioner's land without notice, award, or
payment is unconstitutional, being violative of
Articles 300A, 21 and 14 of the Constitution of
India.
(v) Direct the respondents to complete the
acquisition process in accordance with law, by
issuing a reasoned order within a time frame fixed
by this Hon'ble Court."
5. Learned Standing Counsel, on
instructions submits that National
Highway was constructed in the year
2018; no part of petitioner's land was
acquired and it is not clear whether
road was constructed over petitioner's
land or not.
6. Learned counsel for petitioner,
however, refers to a report issued by
Tehsildar on 25.02.2026, for
contending that petitioner's land was

UKHC010170802026
2026:UHC:8776
affected by construction of road.
7. Since there is a dispute as to
whether petitioner's land is affected by
construction of road or not, which
question cannot be decided in a writ
petition, therefore, the writ petition is
disposed of with liberty to petitioner to
make representation to District
Magistrate, Uttarkashi. If he makes
representation within two weeks,
decision thereupon shall be taken by
District Magistrate concerned, within
four months thereafter. It goes without
saying that National Highway Division
of State Public Works Department shall
also be heard before taking any
decision on petitioner's representation.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 29.09.2026
Navin
